items.title: Replace the named place with *ai*
items.caption: The full place phrase sits at the end. The pointing-back word replaces it and moves directly after the verb, before the doer.

states.label: Place named
states.sm: Sā nofo le teine ʻi le nuʻu.
states.en: The girl lived in the village.

items.title: A fronted place can be copied inside
items.caption: Both printed forms are good Samoan. The pointing-back copy after the verb is common but optional when the place already leads.

states.label: With the copy
states.sm: ʻi le nuʻu sā nofo ai le teine.
states.en: In the village the girl lived there.

states.label: Without the copy
states.sm: ʻi le nuʻu sā nofo le teine.
states.en: In the village the girl lived.

items.title: Sort there and to there
items.intro: Place each complete sentence under the pointing-back form it uses.

items.why: A verb of staying uses the bare pointing-back word here.
The bare form sits after the verb and before the doer.

items.sm: Sā alu le tama ʻi ai.
items.why: A movement toward the goal usually takes the place word before *ai*.

items.sm: Sā alu le teine ʻi ai.
items.why: The two-word form fills the goal slot of the movement verb.
